definition: A picture of how two quantities are related, drawn on axes. Every point $(x, y)$ on the graph fits its equation.
A pair of numbers $(x, y)$ giving the position of a point: $x$ across, then $y$ up.
How steep a line is: the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$, $m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}$.
How far a line goes up (the change in $y$) between two of its points.
How far a line goes across (the change in $x$) between two of its points.
Where a line crosses the $y$-axis. For $y = mx + c$ it is the point $(0, c)$.
A straight line that just touches a curve at one point and has the same gradient as the curve there.
An exact position, given by its coordinates $(x, y)$.
The gradient function of a curve. For $y = x^n$ it is $\frac{dy}{dx} = nx^{n-1}$.
Distance travelled per unit of time. On a distance–time graph it is the gradient.
The area between a curve and the $x$-axis, found by integration.
Lines that never meet. Parallel lines have the same gradient.
A point on a curve where the gradient is $0$.
